description: A facilities manager must decide whether to keep a temperature-sensitive reactor batch running during a central chilled-water pump failure and finalize the temporary cooling, isolation, and safety controls, with input from process engineering, maintenance, and environmental health and safety.

shared_context.S1: The plant's central chilled-water pump P-2 failed during the morning shift, and the affected production areas are currently without their normal cooling capacity.
shared_context.S2: The reactor suite has a scheduled batch today, while the packaging area and utilities workshop also use chilled water.
shared_context.S3: Facilities normally avoids temporary hose connections unless the installation, access, and isolation controls are recorded before use.
shared_context.S4: Before temporary cooling connections are used, facilities conducts a pre-work review of process, maintenance, and environmental health and safety findings.

PF1.text: Jon's process calculation for today's Reactor R batch shows that it requires exactly 400 kW of cooling and a supply temperature no higher than 8 degrees Celsius; he completed the calculation during the batch review but has not entered it in the production control record yet.

PF2.text: Priya confirmed with the rental provider this morning that a temporary chiller rated at exactly 250 kW can arrive today, while Pump P-1 can provide 300 kW after Valve V-17 is isolated; the rental unit requires exactly 6 hours for installation and this vendor confirmation is not yet attached to the maintenance work order.

PF3.text: Owen's site walkthrough found that the temporary chiller hose would cross a marked access lane, so EHS requires barriers maintaining exactly 1.2 meters of clearance and a fire watch during installation; he recorded the finding in his inspection notes, which have not yet been filed with the work permit.

acceptance_conditions: Reactor R's batch must continue in a reduced cooling configuration rather than being cancelled.
The cooling plan must specify exactly 400 kW and a maximum supply temperature of 8 degrees Celsius.
A temporary chiller rated at exactly 250 kW must be authorized.
Pump P-1 must be isolated before supplying the reactor suite.
Temporary chiller installation must be scheduled for exactly 6 hours.
The hose route must preserve exactly 1.2 meters of access clearance.
A fire watch must be assigned during installation.
The process cooling requirement must be cited as justification.
The settlement must explicitly commit to Valve V-17 isolation.
The hose-route safety control must be documented.

decisive_facts.why: The exact 400 kW load and 8-degree Celsius limit change the decision to continue Reactor R with a defined combined cooling approach instead of leaving the batch status and cooling specification unresolved.

The confirmed 250 kW chiller, exact 6-hour installation, and requirement to isolate V-17 for P-1 change the plan to authorize the chiller, schedule six hours, and explicitly commit to P-1 and V-17 isolation.
The hose crossing the access lane changes the safety plan to exactly 1.2 meters of clearance, a fire watch, and an explicitly documented hose-route control.
